runs.question: How does the NIST Generative AI Profile describe data privacy risks?

answer.text:
The retrieved passages don't say how the Generative AI Profile (NIST AI 600-1) describes data privacy risks. The excerpts from that document cover only its cover page, front matter, and acknowledgments, so I can't give its position on privacy.

The passages do show that other NIST publications describe the profile's scope. One says it elaborates risks unique to or exacerbated by generative AI and how to apply the AI RMF to manage them. Another notes that the profile highlights twelve different categories of risk from generative AI in more detail. The excerpts don't list those twelve categories, so I can't say whether privacy is one of them.

The only privacy discussion in the results comes from NIST AI 100-1 (the AI RMF 1.0), which is a different document. It states that AI systems can also present new risks to privacy by allowing inference to identify individuals or previously private information about individuals. This is not the Generative AI Profile's view, so it shouldn't be taken as one.

To answer your question, you would need the sections of AI 600-1 that cover its risk categories, which weren't among the retrieved passages.
